No filesystem access. Alright.
Let me think about level 1's victory condition more carefully. Because level 2's victory condition is probably analogous: "the piece reaches the vicinity of the ball."
Level 1: the piece is a 3x3 purple at (24,37) [t21]. Click (19,44) → level clear. The piece probably moved to (19,44) (the clicked dot) — a 3-step jump? Or did the piece move to the nearest dot on the path toward the click? The dots on the path from (24,37): (23,40), (21,42), (19,44), (17,46). Click (19,44) → the piece moved exactly to the clicked dot (19,44), 3 steps ahead. Hmm, so maybe the piece moves to the clicked dot (any distance) — but then why did it only move 1-2 steps per click in earlier clicks?
t12: click (57,6) → piece (58,3)→(56,5): moved 2 steps toward the click? The clicked dot (57,6) is on the path; the piece moved from (58,3) to (56,5), which is 1 step past (57,6)?? Path: (58,3),(57,6)?? Wait, the path dots: (57,6),(55,8),(53,10),(51,12)... The piece is 3x3 at (58,3) — hmm, the piece's top-left is (58,3), so it covers (58-60, 3-5). The path dot (57,6) is adjacent. After click (57,6): the piece is at (56,5)?? That's not on the path (the path is (55,8)). Hmm, wait, t13: click (17,46) → piece (56,5)→? t14 click (55,8) → piece (54,7). So the piece moved from (56,5) to (54,7) — a diagonal step. The piece's position: (58,3)→(56,5)→(54,7)→(48,13)?? t15: click (49,14) → piece (48,13). That's a 6-step jump! From (54,7) to (48,13): path dots (53,10),(51,12),(49,14)... (48,13) is not on the path. Hmm, the piece's top-left (48,13) covers (48-50,13-15); the path dot (49,14) is at its center! So the piece is centered on the clicked dot (49,14) → top-left (48,13).
So the piece moves to the clicked dot (centered on it), any distance? But t12: click (57,6): if the piece is centered on (57,6), top-left = (56,5). Yes! That matches. t14: click (55,8) → top-left (54,7). Yes. t15: click (49,14) → (48,13). Yes. t16: click (43,20) → (42,19). Yes. t19: click (37,26) → (36,25). Yes. t20: click (31,32) → (30,31). Yes. t21: click (25,38) → (24,37). Yes. t22: click (19,44) → piece centered on (19,44) → top-left (18,43). And the level cleared.
So the level 1 rule: click a dot on the path → the piece teleports to that dot (centered). Victory: piece reaches (19,44)?? Why there? The ball is at (11,44) [59px, minrow=11, mincol=44]. The ball's center is roughly (11+?, 44+?). The ball is 59px, roughly a 7x9 blob: rows 11-18?, columns 44-51? Center is about (14.5, 47.5). The dock G 9px is at (14,47) — the dock is at the ball's center! So the ball is drawn around the dock.
Piece at (19,44) (centered) covers (18-20, 43-45). The dock is at (14,47). Distance from piece center (19,44) to dock (15.5,48.5): about 6. Hmm.
Maybe victory = the piece reaches a dot in the same column as the ball's center column (44)? Or victory = the piece gets within a certain distance of the dock?
Or victory = the piece reaches the dot closest to the dock on the path? The dots: (17,46) distance to dock (15,48) = sqrt(4+4)=2.83; (19,44) distance = sqrt(16+16)=5.66. (17,46) is closer. So it's not "the closest dot."
Maybe victory = the piece's center is in the same column as the ball (column 44)? (19,44) is column 44. The next dot (17,46) is column 46. So victory when the piece is in column 44? That seems arbitrary, but possible: "align the piece with the target's column."
Or victory = the piece is within Chebyshev distance 5 of the ball's center (14.5, 47.5)? Piece center (19,44): Chebyshev = max(4.5, 3.5) = 4.5 ≤ 5. Piece center (21,42): max(6.5,5.5)=6.5 > 5. So victory at distance ≤ 5.
Or victory = the piece reaches a dot such that a straight line to the dock is unobstructed?
I can't pin down the exact rule, but the gist is: the piece moves to the clicked dot, and victory occurs when the piece is close to the ball/dock.
Now level 2: where's the piece?? There's no purple piece on the board! Unless... the piece is the ball, and the ball moves to the clicked dot! But the ball didn't move in my clicks. Hmm, but wait — maybe the ball only moves when the clicked dot is "valid" (e.g., the nearest unmarked dot?). All my clicks were on dots... the ball didn't move.
Or the piece is the yellow 4x4 in the HUD, and the goal is to move it to the ball. How does it move? Clicking a dot creates a marker... no, that's not it.
Or — the piece is invisible/hidden, and clicking a dot reveals it?
Let me look at the level 2 board again: HUD row 0: c background; S(1,1), M(1,5), p(1,9), Y(1,13) 2x2 squares; Y 4x4 at (3,30). Main: b ball 69px at (23,29); 8 S dots.
Level 1's HUD: p 9px at (4,30) — a purple 3x3 in the HUD! And the piece on the board was also a purple 3x3. So the HUD shows a preview of the piece! In level 2, the HUD has a yellow 4x4 at (3,30) — so the piece is a yellow 4x4, but it's not on the board! It's in the HUD. Goal: move the yellow piece from the HUD to the ball?
How? Maybe clicking a dot "places" the piece on the path... but the markers were M (magenta), not yellow.
Hmm, wait. Maybe the 4 squares S, M, p, Y in the HUD are "inventory items," and the yellow 4x4 is the piece. The goal: click a dot to move the piece... no, that's not it.
Let me try: click the yellow 4x4 in the HUD, then click a dot.
